diff --git a/inflection/__init__.py b/inflection/__init__.py
index ffac5ce22e60816f18267d742455e4936b6d1c1a..42aa6cabfac437bfe8f48487633ce7140cbac2db 100644
--- a/inflection/__init__.py
+++ b/inflection/__init__.py
@@ -371,12 +371,51 @@ def titleize(word: str) -> str:
       >>> titleize("raiders_of_the_lost_ark")
       'Raiders Of The Lost Ark'
 
+    Words in all caps, such as acronyms, are kept as they are if the string
+    also has lowercase letters. A string with no lowercase letters, such as a
+    shouted heading, is titleized like any other::
+
+      >>> titleize("NASA rocket launch")
+      'NASA Rocket Launch'
+      >>> titleize("read the HTTP spec")
+      'Read The HTTP Spec'
+      >>> titleize("HELLO WORLD")
+      'Hello World'
+
     """
-    return re.sub(
+    title = re.sub(
         r"\b('?\w)",
         lambda match: match.group(1).capitalize(),
         humanize(underscore(word)).title()
     )
+    if any(char.islower() for char in word):
+        title = _restore_acronyms(word, title)
+    return title
+
+
+def _restore_acronyms(word: str, title: str) -> str:
+    """
+    Put the words of `word` that are in all caps, such as "NASA" or "HTTP",
+    back into `title`, the string that :func:`titleize` made from `word`.
+    """
+    # Split CamelCase words where underscore() does, but keep the case, so
+    # that "NASARocket" gives "NASA" and "Rocket".
+    word = re.sub(r"([A-Z]+)([A-Z][a-z])", r'\1_\2', word)
+    word = re.sub(r"([a-z\d])([A-Z])", r'\1_\2', word)
+    # The title has the same words in the same order, so they pair up one by
+    # one. A trailing "_id" that humanize() dropped is left without a pair.
+    originals: typing.Iterator[str] = iter(re.findall(r"[^\W_]+", word))
+
+    def restore(match: typing.Match[str]) -> str:
+        titled = match.group()
+        original = next(originals, '')
+        # Compare the words too, in case some unusual character changed how
+        # the title splits into words and the pairing is off.
+        if original.isupper() and original.lower() == titled.lower():
+            return original
+        return titled
+
+    return re.sub(r"[^\W_]+", restore, title)
